 \rm \frac{100}{index\ number\ of\ new\ base\ year} **
 
 
• This is the correct formula for base shifting.
 
• It involves multiplying old index numbers by the ratio of 100 to the index number of the new base year.
 
• This ensures the index numbers are adjusted to the new base year.
 
• It maintains consistency and comparability of index numbers over different periods.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: (100 * index number of new base year)**
 
 
• This option is incorrect.
 
• Multiplying by 100 and the index number of the new base year would result in a much larger value.
 
• It doesn't align with the concept of base shifting.
 
• It would distort the index numbers instead of adjusting them.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: (100 * index number of new base year)²**
 
 
• This option is incorrect.
 
• Squaring the product of 100 and the index number of the new base year is not part of the base shifting process.
 
• It would result in an even larger and incorrect value.
 
• This approach does not serve the purpose of adjusting index numbers to a new base year.
